leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer B014 (optical lattice clocks) as a single-achievement prize for Katori and Ye, each with a citation for invention and realisation of the clock; the citations differ only in how they describe the payoff (a new regime of precision time and frequency measurement, 10^-18 performance, or magic-wavelength trapping). They share the scientific case: a conceptual step (magic-wavelength trapping in the Lamb-Dicke regime), reproduction at the 1e-18 level in several laboratories, and a compact two-name credit. They do not share the same weight on the reservations. All six flag overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the not-yet-decided redefinition of the SI second, and the omission of Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and others. Several also record that their support may be inflated by field proximity (Lindroth, Kroll), by B014 being the safest option (Johansson), or by consensus-seeking (the Chair, who moved B014 to the head of his configuration after reading the opening ballots). Their alternatives diverge: B009 and B016 (Johansson), B008 and B016 (Kroll), B008 and B020 (Lindroth), B001 and B017 (Mehlig), B017 and B042 (Olsson), B021 and B016 (Pearce).

Danielsson prefers B021 (IceCube) for Halzen, Spiering and Karle, as a discovery from nature that no one could have predicted in detail, with the diffuse flux seen in several IceCube analysis channels and the TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane results pointing to real accelerators. He ranks B014 first among his alternatives and states plainly that he should not mistake his own support for broad support. The shared ground with the B014 camp is the standard of independent reproduction. The unshared ground is that confirmation here comes from IceCube channels rather than from other detectors, KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are not yet at comparable sensitivity, and the three-name credit omits DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers and other IceCube leaders. Pearce lists B021 as his first alternative but explicitly prefers B014; Johansson would defer to astroparticle colleagues but would not fix the prize on B021; Olsson argues that Spiering must stay in any IceCube credit.

Eriksson prefers B016 (topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect) for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, as a new class of quantum matter defined by topology, with theory (Z2 invariant) and experiment (HgTe edge transport) in one prize and more than fifteen years of independent confirmation in transport and ARPES. He concedes the credit is not clean (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route; the three-dimensional work lies outside the names; Zhang is deceased) and the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces novelty, and says B014 is the cleaner configuration if the committee finds the gap too large. B016 is named as an alternative by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce, but none of them prefers it; Johansson calls it conceptually deepest but ranks it behind B014 for attribution and prior recognition, while Danielsson regards a prize that omits the proposers of the tested experiment as not yet clean.

areas_of_agreement: B014 is the only configuration preferred by more than one member (six of eight), and it is a two-laureate, single-achievement prize in each of those six files.
Members on every side accept that the lattice clock is reproduced across several laboratories at about the 1e-18 level; no member in the eight files disputes the physics of the clocks.

All six B014 supporters name the same three reservations: overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the unfinished SI redefinition of the second, and priority claims by Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and others outside the two names.

Several members say a two-part prize combining B014 with another candidate does not fit the three-person limit (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce), so the live question is a single-achievement prize.
Danielsson and Eriksson, the two members who do not prefer B014, each name it as their first alternative and call it the cleaner attribution (Eriksson explicitly, Danielsson as its main advantage).
Several members state that the accompanying claims (credit history and exact priority dates) are recalled rather than checked, and that they would want expert evaluation before a final ballot.
scientific_disputes: Instrument versus discovery: Danielsson ranks the clock fifth in his opening ballot because he weighs a measuring invention below a discovery from nature, and Eriksson asks whether the clock tells us something new or is an enabling instrument; Kroll and Pearce value a new measurement technique that opens new observations; Johansson points to many-body and gravitational-redshift physics as the new science.

Whether the lattice scheme is a distinct invention or a third prize for one field of precision time (comb 2005, ion control 2012); Lindroth, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce and Johansson all raise this, and the Chair has asked Lindroth to say whether she would defend the distinction against that objection.

Whether the IceCube result is a secure discovery as it stands (Danielsson, Pearce: the diffuse flux is far above five sigma) or whether partial source identification makes it early (Lindroth, Johansson in their files as described by others).

Whether B016 is distinct enough from the 2016 prize on topological phases: Eriksson argues the Z2 invariant, time-reversal-protected edge states and HgTe experiment are separate discoveries; Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson see a precedent that reduces novelty.

Whether B009 (circuit QED) is a new discovery or a continuation of the 2025 prize on macroscopic tunnelling in circuits (Eriksson, Kroll, Pearce as noted in the files); Johansson, who ranked it first in his opening ballot, now accepts the point more than before but still treats the science as real.
attribution_disputes: B014: the credited pair Katori and Ye is defended as having a clear originator and a clear record-performance leader (Johansson, Pearce), but all supporters note that Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and others, and ion-clock groups, are left out; Johansson wants the citation to say invention and realisation so it does not read as credit for the whole community.

B021: Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce question whether a three-person cut from a large collaboration and from the DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA lineage is arbitrary; Olsson argues that dropping Spiering would weaken, not clean, the attribution; no member has proposed a different set of names.

B016: the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased) and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan) lie outside Kane, Mele and Molenkamp; Eriksson and Johansson both call this the serious problem, with different conclusions about whether it is fatal.

B042 and B009 are not preferred by anyone in round 1, but the omission of STEM-corrector originators such as Krivanek (Olsson, Eriksson) and the inseparability of Yale, ETH and Sherbrooke credit from the 2025 laureates (Eriksson) were raised.
maturity_disputes: B014: the SI second has not been redefined. Danielsson would let the clock wait without cost, and Kroll and Eriksson do not regard waiting as obligatory; Danielsson asks whether the pioneers of IceCube should be recognised while they are alive and active.

B021: independent confirmation is within IceCube analysis channels, not across detectors; KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are not yet at comparable sensitivity, which Danielsson and Pearce both acknowledge and others read as a timing issue.
B017: Olsson and Eriksson record that the pairing mechanism and sample variability in twisted bilayer graphene leave open whether recognition is early.
B009: timing relative to the 2025 prize is a maturity question for Kroll, Eriksson and Pearce, although only Johansson prefers to keep it as an alternative.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, Chalmers superconducting-circuit community) discloses close ties to circuit QED and flags B009, and to a lesser extent B008, for recusal consideration; he has discounted his own opening first place for B009 and does not prefer it in round 1. Eriksson has asked him directly whether he should step back from B009.

Olsson discloses that B042 (aberration-corrected electron optics) is in her own field of transmission electron microscopy at Chalmers, ranked it first in the opening ballot, and would recuse from the final decision on B042 or ask colleagues to test her judgement.
Eriksson notes that his DFT and magnetism work is adjacent to B016 and in close proximity to B018 (LDA+DMFT), and asks that this be borne in mind if B018 is discussed.

Lindroth notes that many-body atomic theory brings her close to the clock community and that she may be too fond of B014; she also notes her long-standing collaboration with the 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier concerns a different field.

Kroll notes WACQT leadership (overlapping institutionally with Johansson at Chalmers, relevant to B009) and a general AMO and quantum-information background overlapping with B008, with no named candidate being a direct collaborator; he flags that his bias toward metrology should be discounted for B014.
Mehlig notes he is in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers); he has no collaboration with candidates in B014, B001, B017 or B016.

The Chair (Pearce) works in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, not in IceCube, but KTH astroparticle physics is close to the IceCube field; no recusal seems required, and atomic clocks are outside his own expertise, so he relies on colleagues for B014 priority history. Danielsson and Pearce state no specific conflict for B021 or B014.
questions_for_round2: Lindroth, Kroll and Johansson: is the lattice clock distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize in a way a prize citation can state in one sentence, and is there a draft citation that says invention and realisation without implying credit for the whole clock community?

What is the documented priority history among Katori (magic-wavelength proposal, 2001-2003), Ye (record performance), Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups, and can anyone with reliable knowledge check the dates that members say they recalled rather than verified?

Does the committee want the formal redefinition of the SI second to be decided before the clock is awarded, or is the demonstrated science (reproduction at 1e-18, gravitational-redshift and many-body tests) sufficient on its own?

Danielsson and Eriksson: given that each names B014 as the cleaner attribution, what specific additional fact or change in the credited names would make you prefer your own ballot (B021 or B016) to B014 in the final ballot?

For B021, can the committee request an expert assessment of independent confirmation (KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD) and a historical note on DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA credit, and would Olsson's point that Spiering must stay change the three-person set?

Should any B014-plus-second-part configuration be considered at all given the three-person limit, or should round 2 treat the final ballot as a choice among single-achievement prizes (B014, B021, B016)?
Should Johansson step back from B009 and Olsson from B042 in the final ballot, and does either disclosure affect how the committee should read the alternatives lists?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one configuration with broad explicit support (B014, six of eight members, with Danielsson and Eriksson naming it as their first alternative) and two single-supporter positions (B021 and B016) that each rest on a different weighing of discovery, maturity and credit. Six members support B014 while attaching the same three reservations to it, so round 2 should test those reservations directly instead of counting further. I count only the positions in the eight round-1 files; the Chair's own file shows that his preference moved from IceCube to the clock after reading the opening ballots, and the committee should weigh that disclosure, since agreement on B014 is partly the result of members moving toward it.
